Details.RequiredDocuments:
A complete resume is required. Your resume must show relevant experience, job title, duties and accomplishments. Your resume must show complete information for each job entry to support minimum qualifications. The following information should be provided in your resume, but it is acceptable to provide elsewhere in your application package: employer's name, starting and end dates (Mo/Yr), hours per week, and pay plan, series and grade level (e.g. GS-0201-09) for relevant federal experience.TIP: A good way to ensure you include all essential information is to use the Resume Builder in USAJOBS to create your resume. Are you claiming membership in any professional organizations, or possession of a license, certificate or credentials? Check the Conditions of Employment section above to see if any are required. If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume or assessment questionnaire regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference?
If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents contain personal information such as SSN and DOB and some documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove said personal information before you submit your application. You must provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected.
Details.OtherInformation: COVID VACCINATION INFORMATION: To comply with the recent preliminary nationwide injunction on Executive Order 14043, Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees, the Department of the Navy is not taking any action to implement or enforce the COVID-19 vaccination requirement. New hires will need to provide their vaccination status as well as comply with workplace safety protocols related to masking, physical distancing, testing, travel, and quarantine. This position is covered by the Department of Defense Priority Placement Program. Several vacancies may be filled. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if the selectee fails to meet the pre-employment requirements, including failure to report to any of the scheduled appointments. Federal annuitant information: The selection of an annuitant is subject to the Department of Defense and Department of the Navy policy on the employment of annuitants. Policy information may be found at: http://www.secnav.navy.mil/donhr/Documents/CivilianJobs/FedCivAnnuitants.pdf. Veteran's preference does not apply when selecting individuals under this specific hiring authority. However, if you claim veteran's preference, you will be required to submit supporting documentation with your application as described in the Required Documents section below. This position is subject to work an uncommon tour, including nights, weekends, and holidays to meet mission requirements. Overtime or night differential pay and/or unusual duty hours may be required. The position may require irregular hours and/or rotating shift work. Certain incentives (such as Recruitment, Relocation or Student Loan Repayment) may be authorized to eligible selectees. A relocation incentive is generally a single payment intended to offset some of the relocation costs experienced by the selectee. A relocation incentive may be authorized. This position is eligible for part time, full time or ad-hoc telework at the discretion of management. Vacancies filled from this announcement may be filled at any grade level listed. If selected below the full performance level, you may be noncompetitively promoted to the next higher grade level after meeting all regulatory requirements, and upon the recommendation of management. Promotion is neither implied nor guaranteed.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: For GS-10: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-09) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector designing and fabricating equipment by applying depot level troubleshooting and repair methods associated with electronic and electromechanical equipment and components (e.g., circuit card assemblies, electronics assemblies, cables and wiring harnesses) to ensure reliability and availability. For GS-09: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-08) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector performing repairs associated with electronic equipment and components (e.g., circuit card assemblies, electronics assemblies, cables and wiring harnesses) to ensure reliability and availability. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Individual Occupational Requirements: Electronics Technical Series, 0856 Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Details.JobSummary: You will serve as an Electronics Technician in the Undersea Systems & Sustainment Engineering Department Code 40, Rapid Prototyping and Fabrication Technology Division Code 42, Applied Electronic/Mechanical Branch Code 422, Applied Technology Electronics Section Code 4221 at the Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Keyport ( NAVUNSEAWARCENDIV KEYPORT WA).
Details.SubAgencyName: Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Keyport Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will design and fabricate electronic equipment including: circuit boards, cables, wiring harnesses, electromechanical assemblies and test sets.
You will develop plans, specifications, and instructions, including constructing, assembling, arranging, mounting, and wiring electronic parts and components.
You will make measurements to diagnose malfunctions to ensure equipment operates within prescribed standards
You will install equipment in accordance with developed plans, specifications, and instructions and drawings.
You will perform preventive and corrective maintenance to keep equipment and systems in reliable condition.
You will repair systems and equipment.
You will detect and diagnose malfunctions, tear down equipment, repair or replace parts or components.
You will align, calibrate, and test the modified or repaired equipment.

You will program, operate, and maintain automated surface mount and through hole circuit board manufacturing equipment, including: stencil printers, automated optical inspection machines, vapor flow ovens, and selective solder machines.
You will operate and maintain Electronics assembly calibration and testing, using basic electrical test equipment as well as locally developed test sets and routines.

You will program, operate, and maintain automated wiring harness manufacturing equipment, including automated cutting and stripping machines, automated wire bundle taping machines and wire harness braiding machines.
You will analyze and interoperate test results to determine to provide inputs for troubleshooting and repair processes.
You will assist engineers in the development of production and repair processes.
You will provide input and guidance in the development of manufacturing, testing and repair processes.
You will provide training on subjects, equipment, and processes under your cognizance to contractors, engineers, technicians and end users.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Production Acceptance Engineer (PAE) in the Undersea Warfare Weapons and Product Acceptance Division in the System Acceptance and Operation Readiness Department of Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Keyport (NAVUNSEAWARCENDIV KEYPORT WA).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will be responsible for procurement quality assessment and acceptance testing strategy development, contract language development, and performance monitoring and risk assessment associated with the production of torpedoes and undersea systems.
You will Monitor Contractor, Intermediate Maintenance Activity (IMA), Depot, Underwater Range, and other Program operations for data associated with torpedo/system production hardware.
You will assess available data, evaluate, and prepare status reports and schedules as required to complete project assignments.

You will coordinate with a Technical Project Manager, PA Lead, other PAEs, other engineers within Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Customer Advocates, and/or Contractor personnel for reporting and support of data calls.
You will assist other PAEs in the test strategy planning, analysis, evaluation, and assessment recommendation generation associated with those products under their primary purview.
You will prepare contractual documentation to facilitate proper production acceptance as a part of future procurements.

You will coordinate with technical personnel, where necessary, for the incremental development of weapon production acceptance strategies, requirements verification specifications, and database environments.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Applicants must possess Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Degree: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. 1310-Physics Series: A degree in physics; or a related degree that includes at least 24 semester hours in physics; or, a combination of education and experience demonstrated by coursework that is equivalent to a major in physics (at least 24 semester hours), plus appropriate experience or additional education; 1321-Metallurgy Series: Degree: metallurgy or metallurgical engineering that included at least 20 semester hours in metallurgical subjects; OR a combination of experience and education that equate to one year of experience - courses equivalent to a major in metallurgy or metallurgical engineering that included at least 20 semester hours in metallurgical subjects, plus appropriate experience or additional education. 1520-Mathematics Series: A degree in mathematics or the equivalent of a major that included at least 24 semester hours in mathematics; or, a combination of education and experience demonstrated by courses equivalent to a major in mathematics (including at least 24 semester hours in mathematics, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Your total coursework must have included differential and integral calculus and, in addition, four advanced mathematics courses requiring calculus or equivalent mathematics courses as a prerequisite;

From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will provide technician leadership and coordination during new torpedo system hardware integration, torpedo production, complex system level troubleshooting, and new design initiatives.

You will perform management, production, testing, standardization, monitoring, assembly, troubleshooting and maintenance functions in support of these projects, customer interface, and coordinate efforts ensuring customer requirements are met.
You will participate on Technology Program project teams and interface with internal and external customers, other divisions, other departments, and other activities.
You will provide input to engineers and supervisors to improve subsystems, systems, facilities, and equipment that significantly adds to the weapon system usefulness, reliability and maintainability.

You will develop technical procedures and processes for other technicians to follow and perform walkthroughs of procedures and processes to ensure accuracy and identify areas for improvement and efficiency.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Welcome to Navy Region Northwest, the third largest fleet concentration area in the continental United States. Navy Region Northwest's mission is to support the fleet, fighter and family in order to provide ready Naval forces able to execute our nation's defense. We are military, civil service, and contractor professionals who together operate the Navy's premier shore installations. Situated in one of the most beautiful locations in the world, the area offers a unique setting with a variety of activities and opportunities for service members and their families.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-11) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector as a professional INTERDISCIPLINARY ENGINEER: 1) Development of energy and water conservation projects to manage and reduce utilities consumption and demand; 2) Utilizing data generated by programs such as Defense Utilities Energy Report System (DUERS) to prepare the Secretary of the Navy Shore Installation Energy and Water Management Annual Report; 3) Performing project management on a wide variety of utility engineering and construction projects; and 4) Conducting engineering studies of equipment and services of utility and energy-related systems to determine capabilities, service effectiveness, and operating methods. **NOTE: This experience must be fully and clearly supported in your resume. You must be a fully qualified engineer with a degree in electrical, mechanical, civil, or industrial engineering or directly related engineering degree from an accredited engineering college or university (see Education section). Electrical engineering degrees will result in a 0850 designation and titled Electrical Engineer. Mechanical engineering degrees will result in a 0830 designation and titled Mechanical Engineer. All other engineering degrees will result in a 0801 designation and titled General Engineer. Registration as a Professional Engineer is highly desirable but not required. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series AND https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0800/files/all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite! Are you ready to join our talented team of professionals, work on challenging projects, and receive exceptional benefits, with the added comfort of job security? Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Southeast is a world-class organization responsible for the planning, design, construction, maintenance, and repair of sustainable facilities for our U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, Joint and Department of Defense customers. NAVFAC Southeast is a great place to work! We were recognized by the Chief of Civil Engineers as the "Best of Type - Continental United States Facilities Engineering Command" in FY21 for best overall military facilities construction programs. Your safety is our top priority! Our safety program won the 2021 Chief of Naval Operations Award for Achievement in Safety Ashore, Medium Industrial Command. We care about your success! NAVFAC Southeast encourages both professional and personal growth. Are you ready for the challenge?
MajorDuties: You will analyze energy consumption reports to plan reduction strategies that increase renewable energy use and sustainability.
You will collaborate with project developers on contracting needs for energy projects (e.g., Statement of Work, Request for Proposals, Government Cost Estimates).
You will develop reports of operational data to assist management in making decisions regarding energy conservation projects
You will evaluate audit results to provide feedback on energy project development.
Details.Education: In addition to the one year of specialized experience, applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

MajorDuties: You will develop plans and provide technical direction over complex operations involved with the overhaul, maintenance and installation of reactor plant systems and components on nuclear-powered vessels.
You will coordinate, monitor, review, and integrate engineers, consultants, health physicists, quality control inspectors, mechanics and others in developing work sequences.
You will review engineering and production work to make sure requirements for propulsion plant and other related work are met.
You will discuss and resolve operational and maintenance problems with shipyard personnel.

Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Knowledge of a wide range of multidisciplinary professional engineering concepts, principles, practices, standards, methods, techniques, materials, and equipment to effectively apply advanced engineering theories, principles, and concepts to project development, execution, and advisory services. 2. Knowledge of development engineering methodologies sufficient to apply experimental theories and/or new applications to issues and provide technical advice and direction in support of weapon systems, subsystems, and/or support equipment. 3. Knowledge of systems engineering practices and procedures as they pertain to sustainment, modification, logistics, and production management principles, concepts, policies, and systems. 4. Knowledge of the principles of planning and program management; of standard acquisition regulations, practices, and procedures; and of other engineering disciplines used in support of sustainment, modification, and maintenance programs. 5. Ability to devise and evaluate criteria, parameters, characteristics, and interrelationships for design approaches; to assess the impact of new technology on current systems and processes; and to gather, assemble, and analyze facts, form conclusions, and devise and recommend solutions to problems. May be required to work extended or other than normal duty hours, to include evenings, weekends and may be subject to recall. Incumbent may be required to report to work during base exercises, contingencies or emergency situations. Overtime/comp time/credit hours may be required to accomplish assigned duties. This position has been designated as an acquisition position and is covered by the Acquisition Professional Development Program (APDP). The selectee must meet or be capable of achieving Engineering and Technical Management Practitioner level certification within the defined grace period for that certification level after assignment. The position also requires the employee to engage in acquisition continuous learning activities achieving 80 continuous learning points (CLPs) every 24 months.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: Supervisory Interdisciplinary Physical Scientist General Engineer Chief Test Science Branch
MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Research and Development Directorate (RD)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS 15 , if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service as listed below: This position requires knowledge of multiple aspects of R&D Testing and Evaluation, to include the development of technical requirements from programmatic objectives; the analysis of data collected with complex data acquisition systems. Applicants who are physical scientists or engineer are suitable for this position due to their educational backgrounds. Advanced knowledge in the fields of field testing, weapons effects, force protection, and recognition as an expert in these subjects. Indications of such status include publication of pertinent reports/studies; honors, awards, or other such recognition and leadership in national and international community study groups, or commissions; and demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective liaison contacts with established test, weapons development and research and development organizations. Ability to manage, direct, and supervise subordinates and to plan, organize, administer and prioritize work for a multiprogramming organization. This includes the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with multidisciplinary subject matter specialist in the development of program objectives and methodology, and skill in meeting, dealing, negotiating, or maintaining effective working relationships with diverse individuals and groups. Excellent writing and presentation skills, including experience with senior level groups and/or activities, and the ability to serve as an effective spokesperson for the organization. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0801/1301, series as listed below: For the Engineering Series. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1 , or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.) For the 1301 Series - Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. or Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, Defense Threat Reduction Agency. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as the Test Science Branch Chief which is accountable for overall management of the Branch, developing long-range program goals, plans and objectives for the Branch and is held accountable for the success of support activities of the Test Division. The incumbent ensures test reports are thorough, accurate and in compliance with STI regulations.
Details.SubAgencyName: Research and Development Directorate (RD)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a Supervisory Interdisciplinary Physical Scientist General Engineer Chief Test Science Branch at the GS-0801/1301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Incumbent will promote scientific achievement, in-house research and development, and act as mentor to junior technical members. Maintains current, expert level, knowledge of weapons and development programs in order to provide technical advice on the application of these weapons for the defeat of targets including hardened protective structures, tunnels, conventional facilities, and temporary facilities. The incumbent makes recommendations for field testing, using sub- or full-scale weapons, with realistic targets to meet the requirements of program principals and provides technical oversight for agency field test programs. The incumbent is regularly called upon by senior DTRA management as well as by senior personnel in other federal agencies to use expertise and judgment to resolve/defend highly complex issues and intractable problems regarding weapons effects and weapons testing matters. Provides technical direction and oversight to testing programs designed to provide better understanding of the capabilities and limitations of weapons, provide validation of weapon capabilities, CBRN effects and provide realistic simulations for the development and assessment of weapon effects planning and assessment tools and methods. Incumbent also provides oversight of testing performed to develop and validate counter-terrorism and force protection technologies, and to evaluate military or civilian measures for protection from accidental or intentional CBRN release to include Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Toxic Industrial Materials. Plans work for accomplishment by subordinate units, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares schedules based on consideration of difficulty of requirements and assignments such that the experience, training, and abilities of the staff are effectively utilized to meet organization and customer needs. Provides subordinate supervisors and staff with direction and advice regarding policies, procedures, and guidelines. Reviews and structures organization to optimize use of resources and maximize efficiency and effectiveness of the organization. Balances workload and provides overall direction and vision to the subordinate unit leads on a wide range of technical and administrative issues. Establishes metric and analysis systems for units managed to assess efficiency, effectiveness, and compliance with regulatory procedures.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC) is currently seeking a full-time Supervisory General Engineer to work in the AFWNC Minuteman III (MMIII) Systems Directorate, Lead Project Office (LPO) at Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico. This position is not eligible for full-time or remote telework; local area telework options may be available at the discretion of the hiring manager. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the primary interface for the W78 and W87-0 Project Officers Group (POG) in coordination with United State Air Force (USAF) senior leadership and the Nuclear Weapons Council (NWC). The W78 and W87-0 LPO coordinates all research, development, test, and evaluation activities performed by the USAF and Department of Energy (DOE) on joint nuclear weapons development projects. Lastly, this position is dual-hatted as W78 and W87-0 LPO and the Division Chief (lead) for the MMIII Warheads Division within the MMIII Systems Directorate.
MajorDuties: For additional information on direct hire opportunities with the Air Force please click here. The employee will be part of a dynamic engineering team, working with the Department of Defense (DoD), DOE, and industry leaders. Team members operate at a high-performance pace and develop and maintain a radical teaming-centric culture. This position supports the modernization of the ground-based leg of America's nuclear deterrence program. DUTIES: Serves as the warhead engineering technical authority for the organization in assignments concerning electrical/mechanical systems and subsystems of the W78 and W87-0 warheads, as well as the electrical/mechanical mechanisms and components of related subsystems. Provides technical expertise in the design, development, commission, manufacture, operation, maintenance, and disposal of electrical/mechanical devices, systems, equipment, and components. Recommends changes to the Military Characteristics (MCs), Stockpile-to-Target Sequence (STS), and Interface Control Documentation (ICD) to the NWC and subordinate committees for the W78 and W87-0 warheads. Offers authoritative technical advice to the higher levels of agency management on matters of exceptional importance in continuing or abandoning objectives, goals, and programs. Provides significant and innovative recommendations for advancing specialized programs and methods and evaluates and advises on the feasibility of new technology and state-of-the-art for incorporation into existing systems and equipment. Reviews, prepares, or presents oral and written reports to using commands, Air Force, and DoD leadership. Experience on a multi-functional, dynamic engineering team with diverse stakeholders is also highly desired. Strong background in leading multi-functional and dynamic engineering teams and briefing organization's senior leadership.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS 15 , if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service as listed below: This position requires knowledge of multiple aspects of Testing and Evaluation, to include the development of technical requirements from programmatic objectives; the development and implementation of instrumentation plans; and the analysis of data collected with complex data acquisition systems. Applicants who are electronics engineers, physicists, or physical scientists are suitable for this position due to their educational backgrounds. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0855/1301/1310, series as listed below: For the Engineering Series. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1 , or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.) For the 1301 Series - Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. or Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. For the 1310 Series - Degree: physics; or related degree that included at least 24 semester hours in physics.or Combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In either above, the courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, courses in any two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, Defense Threat Reduction Agency. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as the Test Diagnostic Branch Chief, accountable for overall management of the Branch, developing long-range program goals, plans and objectives for the Branch and is held accountable for the success of support activities of the Test Division.
Details.SubAgencyName: Research and Development Directorate (RD)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a Supervisory Interdisciplinary Physicist/Physical Scientist/Electronics Engineer at the GS-0855/1301/1310-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Promotes scientific achievements, in-house research and development, and acts as mentor to junior technical members. Conceives plans, directs, and conducts laboratory and unique field investigations and experimentation that determine the feasibility, adequacy of design, compatibility with characteristics of, and limitations to equipment concepts, test systems, test procedures, facilities, devices, and equipment. Efforts are directed toward advancing the state-of-the-art, improving productivity, and reducing mission operation costs. Is the Agency Test Diagnostics expert and representative at the various national test sites. Works with other military and government organizations and U.S. and foreign experimenters and contractors to assure acquisition of high quality data for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosives testing. Provides a high degree of creative originality, ingenuity, independent thinking, and technical competence to lead a group of technical and scientific experts from industry, government, and foreign experimenters to reach test objectives. As the recognized authority, plans, advises, schedules, and coordinates advanced concept definition efforts and provides expert scientific consultation for the overall technical objectives and parameters for the conduct of pioneering scientific research investigations relevant to CBRNe diagnostic system, investigation, development, and analysis of new ideas. Supervises a professional staff of non-supervisory military and civilian personnel, and oversees work performed by contractors. Sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares schedules based on consideration of difficulty of requirements and assignments such that the experience, training, and abilities of the staff are effectively utilized to meet organization and customer needs. Reviews and structures organization to optimize use of resources and maximize efficiency and effectiveness of the organization. This position requires knowledge of multiple aspects of Testing and Evaluation, to include the development of technical requirements from programmatic objectives; the development and implementation of instrumentation plans; and the analysis of data collected with complex data acquisition systems. Applicants who are physicists, physical scientists, or electronics engineers are suitable for this position due to their educational backgrounds.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, Defense Threat Reduction Agency. The incumbent will be responsible for designing, formulating, documenting, and executing complex test programs based on the requirement of the Department of Defense and the military services for the defeat of foreign military targets and for the protection of U. S. and allied facilities from the effects of conventional, non-conventional, special, and nuclear weapons.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a GENERAL ENGINEER at the GS-0801-12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Works with the Test Scientist, and Project Manager in program initiation, laying the groundwork for the initial schedule, providing cost estimates, and test requirements for all incoming test projects. Works closely with the Project Manager, Test Coordinator and Test Scientist to ensure the test teams are meeting the test or technology support requirements. Leads test teams in planning, fielding and executing Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD) test events. Assesses customer's test requirements, overseeing test planning, monitoring test article construction, writing statements of work, overseeing the development of the test planning documentation, developing the test execution plans, briefing senior leadership on the progress of the test events, creating and monitoring the test schedule, budget compliance, and supervise the safe execution of the test events. Leads test team through test team meetings, training, and other supporting activities. Responsible for scheduling milestone briefs and leading test team in preparation of milestone presentation packages, ensure briefings are consistent with the required format, and ensure fielding and execution are conducted in strict accordance with approved budget and execution plans. Responsible for developing the required schedules, milestones and has a complete understanding of the test schedule and budget status.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: Lead Interdisciplinary Electronics Eng/Chemical Eng/Nuclear Eng/General Eng/Physical Scientist
MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Research and Development Directorate (RD)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS 14 , if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service as listed below: Expert knowledge in engineering and scientific background in order to effectively conduct research into all aspects of CBRNE instrumentation systems. Measurements include: motion measurements (acceleration, velocity, displacement), force/strain/stress measurements, thermal measurements (temperature, thermal flux, IR spectrum camera), and chemical/biological plume measurement (sampler, point and standoff detector). In addition, measurements also include: radiation measurement (radiological detectors), optical measurement (high-speed cameras), power monitoring (current and voltage probe), RF measurements (EM antenna, magnetometer), seismic/acoustic measurements (infrasound, seismometer, geophone, triaxial accelerometer), and pressure measurements. Expert knowledge in basic physics, chemistry, electrical, computer programming languages (i.e. C++, Javascript, Python), nuclear radiation, and mechanical engineering in order to create an instrumentation system resulting in the acquisition of data fulfilling the test measurement requirements. Skill in computer, electrical, electronic, mechanical subsystems, sensors and feedback principles, hardware, and software. You may qualify at the GS 13 , if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service as listed below: Serves as the DTRA WMD instrumentation development expert, and principal investigator and manager within the areas of CWMD and chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and high explosive (CBRNE) programs. Responsible for fielding pressure/accelerometer/stress/strain sensors, aerosol samplers/detectors, and radiological detectors in harsh and/or explosive environments. Oversees installation and maintenance operational checks of digital and analog data acquisition systems (DAS) and associated subsystems. Performs system operational checkouts, implements changes, and reports to the test team for status and performance reporting. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0801/0840/0855/0893/1301, series as listed below: For the Engineering Series. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1 , or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.) For the 1301 Series - Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. or Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. For the 1301 Series Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. Or Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, Defense Threat Reduction Agency. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as the DTRA WMD instrumentation development expert, and principal investigator and manager within the areas of CWMD and chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and high explosive (CBRNE) programs.
Details.SubAgencyName: Research and Development Directorate (RD)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a Lead Interdisciplinary Electronics Eng/Chemical Eng/Nuclear Eng/General Eng/Physical Scientist at the GS-0801/0840/0855/0893/1301-13/14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Responsible for fielding pressure/accelerometer/stress/strain sensors, aerosol samplers/detectors, and radiological detectors in harsh and/or explosive environments. Oversees installation and maintenance operational checks of digital and analog data acquisition systems (DAS) and associated subsystems. Performs system operational checkouts, implements changes, and reports to the test team for status and performance reporting. Interfaces to develop and deploy a complete computer system to be employed in a broad range of applications, including remote data and video transmission communications and computer platform support requirements. This includes real-time bomb damage assessment (BDA); chemical and biological measurement and assessment; environmental, safety and health (ES&H) assessments, and other requirements arising through the test planning process. Researches and uses technical expertise to make sound judgment practices for acquisition of data acquisition systems, video camera imagery systems, materials, and subsystem components for research and development programs. Conceives, plans, directs, and conducts laboratory and unique field investigations. Conducts experimentation that analyzes, tests, evaluates, and/or validates the feasibility, adequacy of design, compatibility with characteristics of and limitations to equipment concepts, test systems, test procedures, facilities, devices, and personnel, based on system or operational requirements. Efforts are directed toward advancing the state-of-the-art, improving productivity, and reducing mission operation costs. Uses advanced theory, concepts, and original approaches to the experimental development process as employed in advancing the state of the art of chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosives (CBRNE) defense research. Advises and consults with all levels of management, headquarters personnel, and other federal agencies, on technical and resource requirements in the design and construction of systems, facilities and/or equipment. Provides a high degree of creative originality, ingenuity, independent thinking, and technical competence to lead a group of technical and scientific experts from industry, government, and foreign experimenters to meet the test objective. Conducts technical reviews, performs programmatic analysis, assessments, and modifies resource allocations, as required. Serves as the DTRA instrumentation development expert and representative at the various national test sites. Works with other military and government organizations, U.S. and foreign experimenters, and contractors to assure acquisition of high-quality data. Monitors overall efficiency of administrative and logistics support, training programs, manpower and financial concerns, safety standards, and contractor performance in support of the division's programs. Manages, coordinates, reviews, and provides expert instrumentation engineering advice to leading scientists relative to CBRNE testing. Plans, manages resources, directs staff, and contractor efforts to develop, procure, maintain and operate equipment and systems needed to provide instrumentation support. The incumbent is responsible for the successful performance testing of instrumentation systems in response to expected extreme conditions encountered in DTRA test environments (e.g., blast, strong shock, etc.). Evaluates proposals for contracts to provide state-of-the-art fiber optic, digital acquisition and digital processing equipment as necessary to support instrumentation goals Plans, advises, schedules, and coordinates advanced concept definition efforts. Provides expert scientific consultation for the overall technical objectives in the conduct of pioneering scientific research investigations relevant to CBRNE diagnostic systems. Uses creativity to identify instrumentation solutions to unique and unexpected problems to CBRNE threat conditions simulated during test and evaluation events. Routinely consults with senior scientists of DTRA, Department of Energy, national, and commercial laboratories on the newest and most complex electronic instrumentation and conducts Instrumentation Workshops. Works with the military, government organizations, foreign partners, and contractors to assure acquisition of high quality data. Monitors the overall efficiency of administrative and logistic support, training programs, manpower, financial concerns, safety standards, and contractor performance in support of the department's programs.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a CHEMICAL ENGINEER OR CHEMIST (INTERDISCIPLINARY) in the LABORATORY DIVISION, QUALITY ASSURANCE OFFICE with the PORTSMOUTH NAVAL SHIPYARD.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will coordinate work efforts with other organizations to complete test programs.
You will plan and conduct chemical and instrumental studies of a very complex and difficult nature in support of regulatory requirement.
You will perform duties needed to comply with hazardous material, hazardous waste, and safety requirements and regulations.
You will advise on improvement of instrumentation or procedural methods.
You will provide technical review and studies of established and/or proposed analytical methods and those recommended by private industry/scientific organizations.
You will perform work to support maintenance of the laboratory quality control program.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: A transcript must be submitted with your application. Chemical Engineering Series, 0893 Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above)ORSuccessful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. Chemistry Series, 1320 Successful completion of a physical sciences, life sciences, or engineering degree that included 30 semester hours in chemistry, supplemented by course work in mathematics through differential and integral calculus, and at least 6 semester hours of physics.
